translations.text: King David was old and advanced in years. They covered him with clothes, but he could not get warm.
His servants said, “Let a young virgin be sought for our lord the king. Let her stand before the king and care for him, and let her sleep beside him so that our lord the king may get warm.”
They searched for a beautiful young woman throughout the territory of Israel. They found Abishag the Shunammite and brought her to the king.
The young woman was very beautiful. She kept the king warm and attended to him, but the king did not have sexual relations with her.
Adonijah son of Haggith exalted himself, saying, “I will be king.” He provided himself with chariots and horsemen and fifty runners to run ahead of him.
His father did not restrain him and never said, “Why have you done this?” He was handsome in appearance, and he was born after Absalom.
He held discussions with Joab son of Zeruiah and with Abiathar the priest, and they supported Adonijah.
But Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, Nathan the prophet, Shimei, Rei, and David’s mighty men did not side with Adonijah.

Adonijah sacrificed sheep, oxen, and lambs by the stone of Zoheleth, which is near the land of Rogel. He invited all his brothers, the king’s sons, and all the men of Judah who were the king’s servants.
But he did not invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty men, or his brother Solomon.
Nathan the prophet spoke to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, and said, “Have you not heard that Adonijah son of Haggith has become king, and our lord King David does not know?
Now come, let me give you advice, so that you may save your own life and the life of your son Solomon.

Go in to King David, speak to him, and say, ‘Did you not, my lord the king, swear to your servant and say, “Your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne”? Why, then, has Adonijah become king?’
While you are still there speaking with the king, I will come in and confirm your words.”
Bathsheba went in to the king in his chamber. The king was very old, and Abishag the Shunammite was attending to him.
Bathsheba bowed down and paid homage to the king. The king said, “What is the matter?”
She said, “My lord the king, you swore to your servant by the Lord your God and said, ‘Your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne.’
But now Adonijah has become king, and you, my lord the king, do not know.
He has sacrificed many cattle, sheep, and lambs, and he has invited all the king’s sons, Abiathar the priest, and Joab the commander of the army. But he has not invited your servant Solomon.
My lord the king, the eyes of all Israel are on you, to tell them who will sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.
When my lord the king sleeps with his ancestors, my son Solomon and I will be considered guilty.”
While she was still speaking with the king, Nathan the prophet arrived.
The king was told, “Here is Nathan the prophet.” He came in before the king and paid homage to him, with his face to the ground.
Nathan said, “My lord the king, did you say, ‘Adonijah will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne’?

For he has gone down today and sacrificed many cattle, sheep, and lambs. He has invited all the king’s sons, the commanders of the army, and Abiathar the priest. They are now eating and drinking before him and saying, ‘Long live King Adonijah!’
But he has not invited me, your servant, or Zadok the priest, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, or your servant Solomon.
Was this matter brought about by my lord the king, and did you not tell your servant who would sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?
King David answered, saying, “Call Bathsheba to me.” She came in before him and stood in his presence.
The king swore, saying, “As the Lord lives, who has rescued my life from every trouble,
just as I swore to you by the Lord, the God of Israel, saying, ‘Your son Solomon will reign after me, and he will sit on my throne in my place,’ so I will surely do this very day.”
Bathsheba bowed with her face to the ground and paid homage to the king, saying, “May my lord King David live forever!”
King David said, “Call Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah son of Jehoiada to me.” They came in before the king.
The king said to them, “Take your lord’s servants with you, have my son Solomon ride on my mule, and bring him down to Gihon.
There Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet shall anoint him king over Israel. Blow the horn and say, ‘Long live King Solomon!’
Then come up after him, and he shall enter and sit on my throne. He shall reign in my place, for I have commanded that he be ruler over Israel and Judah.”
Benaiah son of Jehoiada answered the king, saying, “May it be so! May the Lord, the God of my lord the king, confirm it.
As the Lord has been with my lord the king, may he also be with Solomon, and may he make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David.”
Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites went down. They had Solomon ride on King David’s mule and brought him to Gihon.
Zadok the priest took the horn of oil from the tent and anointed Solomon. He blew the horn, and all the people said, “Long live King Solomon!”
All the people came up after him, dancing and rejoicing with great joy, and the earth resounded with their voices.
Adonijah and all his guests heard it, and they finished eating. Joab heard the sound of the horn and said, “What is this noise resounding in the city?”
While he was still speaking, Jonathan son of Abiathar the priest arrived. Adonijah said, “Come in, for you are a worthy man and bring good news.”
Jonathan answered Adonijah, saying, “Most certainly, our lord King David has made Solomon king.
The king sent Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, Benaiah son of Jehoiada, the Cherethites, and the Pelethites with him, and they had him ride on the king’s mule.
Zadok the priest and Nathan the prophet anointed him king at Gihon. They came up from there rejoicing, and the city resounded. That is the noise you heard.
Solomon has taken his seat on the royal throne.

The king’s servants came in to bless our lord King David, saying, ‘May God make the name of your son Solomon greater than your name, and may he make his throne greater than your throne.’ The king bowed in worship from his bed.
The king said, ‘Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, who today has granted that one of my offspring should sit on my throne, while my own eyes see it.’”
All Adonijah’s guests were frightened, rose, and went away, each on his own way.
Adonijah was afraid of Solomon. He got up, went, and took hold of the horns of the altar.
Solomon was told, “Adonijah is afraid of King Solomon and is holding on to the horns of the altar, saying, ‘Let King Solomon swear to me today that he will not kill his servant with the sword.’”
And Solomon said, “If he proves to be a worthy man, not one hair of his head shall fall to the ground. But if evil is found in him, he shall surely die.”
King Solomon sent for him and had him brought down from the altar. He came and bowed to the ground before King Solomon, and Solomon said to him, “Go to your house.”
And the time drew near for David to die, and he addressed Solomon his son and said:
“I am going the way of all the earth. Be strong and be a man.

Keep the charge of the Lord your God, walking in his ways and keeping his commandments, his ordinances, his judgments, and his testimonies written in the law of Moses, so that you may understand what you are to do according to everything I command you.

Then the Lord will establish his word that he spoke concerning me, saying, ‘If your sons guard their ways, walking before me faithfully with all their heart and all their soul,’ he said, ‘there shall always be a man on the throne of Israel.’

You yourself know what Joab son of Zeruiah did to me, what he did to the two commanders of Israel’s armies, Abner son of Ner and Amasa son of Jether. He killed them and sought the blood of war in peacetime, and put innocent blood [?] at his waist and on the sandals on his feet.
Act according to your wisdom, and do not let his gray hair go down to the realm of the dead in peace.
Show kindness to the sons of Barzillai the Gileadite, and let them be among those who eat at your table, for they came to my aid in this way when I fled from your brother Absalom.

And look, with you is Shimei son of Gera, son of Jemini, from Bahurim. He cursed me with bitter curses on the day when I was going to Mahanaim. But he came down to meet me at the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, saying, ‘I will not kill you with the sword.’
Now do not hold him guiltless, for you are a wise man. You will know what to do to him, and you shall bring his gray hair down to the realm of the dead with bloodshed.”
And David slept with his fathers and was buried in the City of David.
The time David reigned over Israel was forty years. He reigned seven years in Hebron and thirty-three years in Jerusalem.
And Solomon sat on the throne of David his father at twelve years of age, and his kingdom was firmly established.
And Adonijah son of Haggith came to Bathsheba, Solomon’s mother, and bowed down to her. She said, “Do you come in peace?” And he said, “In peace.”
He said, “I have something to say to you.” She said, “Speak.”
And he said to her, “You yourself know that the kingdom was mine, and all Israel looked to me to be king. But the kingdom turned away and became my brother’s, for it became his from the Lord.
Now I ask one favor of you. Do not turn your face away from me.” And Bathsheba said to him, “Speak.”
And he said to her, “Speak to King Solomon, for he will not turn his face away from you, and ask him to give me Abishag the Shunammite as my wife.”
And Bathsheba said, “Very well. I will speak to the king on your behalf.”

And Bathsheba came to King Solomon to speak to him about Adonijah. The king rose to meet her and kissed her, then sat on his throne. A throne was set for the king’s mother, and she sat at his right hand.
And she said to him, “I ask one small favor of you. Do not turn your face away from me.” And the king said, “Ask, my mother, for I will not turn my face away from you.”
And she said, “Let Abishag the Shunammite be given to your brother Adonijah as his wife.”

King Solomon answered his mother and said, “Why do you ask for Abishag the Shunammite for Adonijah? Ask for the kingdom for him as well, for he is my older brother, and with him are Abiathar the priest and Joab son of Zeruiah, the commander and friend.”
King Solomon swore by the Lord and said, “May God do so to me, and more besides, if Adonijah has not spoken these words against his own life.”
And now, as the Lord lives, who made me and placed me on the throne of David my father, and who established a house for me, just as the Lord promised, Adonijah shall surely die this very day.
King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, who killed him, and Adonijah died that day.

The king said to Abiathar the priest, “Go to Anathoth, to your estate, for you deserve death today. But I will not kill you, because you carried the ark of the Lord’s covenant before my father, and because you suffered wherever my father suffered.”
Solomon removed Abiathar from being the Lord’s priest, fulfilling the word of the Lord that he had spoken concerning the house of Eli in Shiloh.
The news reached Joab, for Joab had joined Adonijah and had not sided with Solomon. Joab fled to the Lord’s tent and grasped the horns of the altar.

Solomon was informed, and they said, “Joab has fled to the Lord’s tent, and he is holding the horns of the altar.” Solomon sent word to Joab, saying, “What happened to you that you fled to the altar?” Joab said, “I was afraid of you and fled to the Lord.” Then King Solomon sent Benaiah son of Jehoiada, saying, “Go, kill him and bury him.”

Benaiah son of Jehoiada went to Joab in the Lord’s tent and said to him, “This is what the king says: Come out of there.” Joab said, “I will not come out, for I will die here.” Benaiah son of Jehoiada returned and spoke to the king, saying, “This is what Joab said, and this is the answer he gave.”
The king said to him, “Go and do to him as he said. Kill him and bury him, and today you will remove from me and from my father’s house the guilt for the innocent blood that Joab shed.

The Lord brought the blood of his wrongdoing back upon his own head, because he attacked two men more righteous and braver than himself and killed them with the sword, without my father knowing of their bloodshed: Abner son of Ner, the commander of Israel’s army, and Amasa son of Jether, the commander of Judah’s army.
Their blood came back upon his head and upon the heads of his descendants forever. But may there be peace from the Lord forever for David, his descendants, his house, and his throne.”
Benaiah son of Jehoiada went out, struck Joab, and killed him. He buried him at his own house in the wilderness.

The king appointed Benaiah son of Jehoiada as commander in his place, and the kingdom was established in Jerusalem. The king appointed Zadok the priest in place of Abiathar as priest before the Lord. The Lord gave Solomon very great understanding and wisdom, and breadth of mind like the sand along the seashore. Solomon’s understanding surpassed that of all the descendants of the ancients and the wisdom of the Egyptians. He married Pharaoh’s daughter and brought her into the City of David until he finished building his own house. First he built the house of the Lord and the wall all around Jerusalem, completing them in seven years. Solomon had seventy thousand burden bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains. Solomon made the Sea, the supports, the large basins, the pillars, the fountains of the portico, and the bronze Sea. He built the raised terrace with monuments and separated off the City of David. Then Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the City of David to her own house, which he had built for her, and then he built the raised terrace. Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the Lord, and he burned incense before the Lord. He completed the house. These were the officials overseeing Solomon’s work: three thousand six hundred supervisors of the people who did the work. He built Hazor, Megiddo, Gezer, Upper Beth-horon, and Baalath. But it was after he had built the house of the Lord and the wall all around Jerusalem that he built those cities. While David was still alive, he commanded Solomon, saying, “Look, you have with you Shimei son of Gera, a son of the line of Benjamin, from Hebron. He cursed me with grievous curses on the day when I went to Mahanaim. He came down to meet me on the bank of the Jordan, and I swore to him by the Lord, ‘You shall not die by the sword.’ Now do not treat him as innocent, for you are a wise man and will know what to do to him. Bring his gray hair down to the realm of the dead in blood.”
The king sent for Shimei and summoned him, and said to him, “Build yourself a house in Jerusalem and live there. Do not leave there to go anywhere.”
“On the day you leave, if you cross the Kidron ravine, know for certain that you will surely die, and your blood will be on your own head.” The king swore to him that day.
Shimei said to the king, “What you have said is good, my lord the king. Your servant will do as you have said.” Shimei lived in Jerusalem for three years.
After three years, two of Shimei’s servants fled to Achish son of Maacah, king of Gath. Shimei was informed, “Look, your two servants are in Gath.”
Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and went to Achish to look for his servants. Shimei went and brought his servants back from Gath.
Solomon was told, “Shimei went from Jerusalem to Gath and brought his servants back.”

The king sent for Shimei and summoned him, and said to him, “Did I not make you swear by the Lord and warn you, saying, ‘On the day you leave Jerusalem and go to the right or to the left, know for certain that you will surely die’? And you said to me, ‘What I have heard you say is good.’”
“And now, why have you not kept the oath sworn by the Lord and the command that I gave you?”
The king said to Shimei, “You yourself know the evil that your heart knows you did to David my father. The Lord has brought your evil deeds back upon your own head.”
“But King Solomon is blessed, and David’s throne is established before the Lord forever.”
King Solomon gave the order to Benaiah son of Jehoiada. He went out and struck Shimei down, and he died.

When Solomon’s kingdom was established, Solomon made a marriage alliance with Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and married his daughter. He brought her into the City of David until he finished building his own house, the house of the Lord, and the wall around Jerusalem.
However, the people burned incense at the high places, because no house had yet been built for the name of the Lord.
Solomon loved the Lord and followed the commands of his father David, except that he too offered sacrifices and burned incense at the high places.
The king arose and went to Gibeon to sacrifice there, because it was the greatest and highest high place. Solomon offered a thousand burnt offerings on that altar.
At Gibeon the Lord appeared to Solomon in a dream at night, and the Lord said to Solomon, “Ask for something for yourself.”

Solomon said, “You showed great mercy to my father David, just as he walked before you in truth, righteousness, and uprightness of heart toward you. You preserved this great mercy for him by giving his son a seat on his throne, as it is today.
“And now, Lord my God, you have placed your servant in place of David my father. But I am a little child and do not know how to go out or come in.”
Your servant is among your people whom you chose, a people so numerous that they cannot be counted or numbered.
Give your servant a heart that listens, so that I may judge your people righteously and distinguish between good and evil. For who can judge this great people of yours?”
It pleased the Lord that Solomon had asked for this.

The Lord said to him, “Because you asked me for this, and did not ask for a long life for yourself, or wealth for yourself, or the lives of your enemies, but asked for understanding to listen to matters of justice,
I have done as you asked. I have given you a wise and discerning heart, so that no one like you has existed before you, and no one like you will arise after you.
I have also given you what you did not ask for: wealth and glory, so that no king will be like you throughout your lifetime.
And if you walk in my ways, keeping my commands and commandments as your father David did, I will lengthen your life.”

Solomon awoke, and it had been a dream. He arose and came to Jerusalem, and stood before the altar facing the ark of the Lord’s covenant in Zion. He offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and held a great feast for himself and all his servants.
Then two women who were prostitutes appeared before the king and stood before him.
One woman said, “Please, my lord, this woman and I lived in the same house, and I gave birth in the house.
On the third day, this woman also gave birth. We were alone; no one else was with us in the house except the two of us.
This woman’s son died during the night because she lay on him.
“She rose in the middle of the night and took my child from my arms while your servant was asleep. She laid him in her own bosom and laid her dead son in my bosom.”
I got up in the morning to nurse my son, and he was dead. But when I looked at him in the morning light, he was not the son I had borne.”

The other woman said, “No, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.” But the first woman said, “No, my son is the living one, and your son is the dead one.” So they spoke before the king.
The king said to them, “You say, ‘This living child is my son, and her son is the dead one,’ and you say, ‘No, your son is the dead one, and my son is the living one.’”
The king said, “Bring me a sword.” And they brought a sword before the king.
The king said, “Cut the living infant in two, and give half to this woman and half to the other.”

The woman whose son was alive answered the king, because her heart was deeply stirred for her son. She said, “Please, my lord, give her the living child, and do not kill him!” But the other woman said, “Let him be neither mine nor hers. Cut him in half!”
The king answered, “Give the living child to the woman who said, ‘Give him to her, and do not kill him.’ She is his mother.”
All Israel heard the judgment that the king had given, and they stood in awe of the king, because they saw that the wisdom of God was in him to administer justice.
King Solomon reigned over Israel.
These were his officials: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;
Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, were scribes, and Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud was in charge of the records;
Benaiah son of Jehoiada was in charge of the army, and Zadok and Abiathar were priests;
Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the administrators, and Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king’s friend;
Ahishar was the commander, Eliak was commander of a thousand, Eliab son of Shaph was governor, and Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the tribute.
Solomon had twelve administrators over all Israel who supplied provisions for the king and his household, each for one month of the year.
These are their names: Bein son of Uri, in the hill country of Ephraim;
one, the son of Deker, in Michmash, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh, and Aijalon as far as Beth-hanan;
the son of Hesed, in Arubboth; Socoh and all the land of Hepher belonged to his district;
the son of Abinadab, over all Naphath-dor; Taphath, Solomon’s daughter, was his wife;
Baanah son of Ahilud, over Taanach, Megiddo, and all Beth-shan, which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel, and from Beth-shan as far as Abel-meholah and as far as Mambragha;

Jekmaal son of Geber, in Ramoth-gilead; his district included Havvoth-jair, belonging to Jair son of Manasseh, in Gilead, and the region of Argob in Bashan, sixty large walled cities with bronze bars;
Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;
Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he married Basemath, Solomon’s daughter;
Baanah son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;
Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;
Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;
Geber son of Ara, in the land of Gilead, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan; [?] in the land.
Judah and Israel were as numerous as the sand on the seashore. They ate and drank and rejoiced.
Solomon ruled over the kingdoms from the River through the land of the Philistines to the borders of Egypt. They brought tribute and served Solomon all the days of his life.
These were Solomon’s provisions for one day: thirty cors of fine flour and forty cors of white flour;
ten choice oxen, twenty pasture-fed cattle, and a hundred sheep, besides deer, gazelles, and the choicest fattened birds.
For he ruled over everything beyond the river, from Tiphsah to Gaza, over all the kingdoms on that side of the river. He had peace on every side around him.
Judah and Israel lived securely, each under his own vine and his own fig tree, eating and drinking, from Dan to Beersheba, all the days of Solomon.
Solomon had forty thousand mares for his chariots and twelve thousand riding horses.
In this way Solomon’s royal officials supplied provisions and everything required for the king’s table, each in his assigned month, and they failed to supply nothing.
Likewise, they brought barley and straw for the riding horses and the chariot horses to the place where the king was, each according to his assigned share.
The Lord gave Solomon wisdom, very great understanding, and a breadth of mind like the sand along the seashore.
Solomon’s wisdom far surpassed the understanding of all the people of old and of all the wise men of Egypt.
He was wiser than all people, wiser than Ethan the Zerahite, Heman, Calcol, and Darda, the sons of Mahol. He was famous among all the surrounding nations.
Solomon spoke three thousand proverbs, and his hymns numbered five thousand.
He spoke about trees, from the fir tree in Lebanon to the hyssop that grows out of the wall. He also spoke about animals, birds, and fish.
People from all nations came to hear Solomon’s wisdom, sent by all the kings of the earth who had heard of his wisdom.
Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, because he heard that they had anointed him king in place of David his father, for Hiram had always loved David.
Solomon sent word to Hiram, saying:
You yourself know that David my father could not build a house for the name of the Lord my God because of the wars that surrounded him, until the Lord put his enemies under his feet.
But now the Lord my God has given me rest on every side, and there is neither an adversary nor any evil occurrence.

And now I intend to build a house for the name of the Lord my God, just as the Lord God spoke to David my father, saying, ‘Your son, whom I will place on your throne in your stead, will build a house for my name.’

Now give orders for timber to be cut for me in Lebanon. My servants will be with your servants, and I will pay you the wages for your servants’ work according to whatever you say. For you yourself know that none of our men knows how to cut timber like the Sidonians.
When Hiram heard Solomon’s words, he rejoiced greatly and said, ‘Blessed be the Lord God today, who has given David a wise son to rule over that great people.’
Hiram sent word to Solomon, saying, ‘I have heard everything you sent to tell me. I will fulfill all your wishes concerning fir and cedar timber.

My servants will bring it down from Lebanon to the sea, and I will make it into rafts on the sea and send it to the place you designate to me. I will bring it ashore, and you will take it away. In return, you will fulfill my wish by supplying food for my household.’
Hiram supplied Solomon with fir and cedar timber, fulfilling all his wishes.
Solomon gave Hiram twenty thousand cors of wheat and twenty thousand jars of pressed oil. Solomon gave this to Hiram each year.
The Lord gave Solomon wisdom, just as he had promised him. There was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and they made a covenant with each other.
King Solomon imposed a forced-labor levy on all Israel, and the levy amounted to thirty thousand men.
He sent them to Lebanon in shifts of ten thousand a month. They spent one month in Lebanon and two months at home. Adoniram was in charge of the levy.
Solomon had seventy thousand burden-bearers and eighty thousand stonecutters in the mountains,
besides the supervisors Solomon appointed over the work: three thousand five hundred who oversaw the people doing the work.
The king gave orders, and they brought great blocks of stone, valuable stones for the foundation of the house, and unhewn stones.
Solomon’s sons, Hiram’s sons, and the people of Byblos cut them, and for three years they prepared the timber and stone to build the house.
In the four hundred and fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of King Solomon’s reign over Israel, in the second month, he began building the house of the Lord.
The house that King Solomon built for the Lord was sixty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high.
The vaulted porch in front of the house was twenty cubits long, corresponding to the height of the house, and ten cubits wide in front of the house. He built the house and completed it.
He made windows in the house for looking out, with coverings.
He built an enclosing structure all around the walls of the house, along the walls of both the temple and the inner sanctuary, and made side chambers all around.

The lowest side chamber was five cubits wide, the middle one six cubits wide, and the third seven cubits wide. For he made offsets around the outside of the house, so that the beams would not be driven into the walls of the house.
When the house was being built, it was built with rock and unworked stones, and no hammer or anything made of iron sounded during its construction.
The entrance to the side chamber was below, on the right side of the house. A winding stairway led up to the middle story, and from the middle to the third story.
He built the house and completed it, and covered the house with planking, beams, and frameworks of fir wood.
He built vaulted chambers throughout the house, five cubits high, and covered the vaulted chambers with fir wood.
The word of the Lord came to Solomon, saying:

“As for this house that you are building, if you walk according to my ordinances, carry out my judgments, and keep all my commandments, walking in them, I will establish with you my word that I spoke to David your father.
And I will dwell among the children of Israel and will not abandon my people Israel.”
Solomon built the house and completed it.

He built the walls inside the house with fir wood, from the floor of the house up to the walls and the beams. He covered the interior all around with wood and covered the floor of the house with cedar panels.
He built one side chamber twenty cubits long at the end of the wall, from the floor of the house to the beams, and made the inner sanctuary on its inner side as the Holy of Holies.
The house, the inner temple, was forty cubits long.
He covered the inside of the house with fir wood—the arches, the vaults, and all the carvings were of fir wood—and no stone was visible.
He prepared the area in front of the inner sanctuary, inside the middle of the house, to place the ark of the Lord’s covenant there.
The space before the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits long, twenty cubits wide, and twenty cubits high. He overlaid it with refined gold and made an altar of fir wood.
Solomon covered the inside of the house with pure gold, fastened it with gold nails in front of the inner sanctuary, and covered it with gold.
He coated the entire house with gold until the whole house was finished, and covered the entire interior of the inner sanctuary with gold plates.
Inside the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of cypress wood; one measured ten cubits in size.
One of its wings was five cubits long, and its second wing was five cubits long: ten cubits from one wingtip to the other.
The second cherub was the same; the cherubim had the same measurements and the same overall dimensions.
The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and the second cherub was the same.

He placed the two cherubim in the middle of the inner house and spread out their wings. One cherub’s wing reached one wall, and the second cherub’s wing reached the other wall. Their wings met wingtip to wingtip in the middle of the house.
He covered the cherubim with gold.
On all the walls of the house, all around, he carved with a carving tool cherubim, palm trees, and carved designs [?], in both the innermost and the outer parts.
He covered the floor of the house with gold, both the inner and the outer parts.
For the entrance to the inner sanctuary he made doors of juniper wood and fivefold doorframes.
There were two doors of cedar wood, with attached carvings of cherubim, palm trees, and outspread petals. He covered them with gold, and the gold ran down over the cherubim and palm trees.
In the same way, he made four-sided doorposts of juniper wood for the entrance to the temple.
For the two entrances he made cedar doors, each door having two leaves, and their hinges were double.
The second door had a frame, with cherubim, palm trees, and open flower petals carved on it, and was covered with gold laid over the carved work.
He built the inner courtyard with three courses of dressed stone and a wall made of fir wood.
In the fourth year, in the month of Ziv, the second month, the foundation of the house of the Lord was laid.
In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was completed in all its details and according to its entire design. He spent seven years building it.
Solomon spent thirteen years building his own house, and he completed his entire house.
He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, one hundred cubits long, fifty cubits wide, and thirty cubits high, with three rows of fir-wood pillars and fir-wood beams upon the pillars.
He roofed the house above the side chambers of the pillars. The number of pillars was forty-five, fifteen in each row.
There were three frames, and openings faced openings in three rows.
All the doorways and all the openings were square and framed, with doorway facing doorway in three rows.
He made the portico of pillars fifty cubits long and thirty cubits wide. The porticoes were joined opposite one another, and the pillars and their bases stood in front of the porticoes.
He made the portico of the thrones, where he judged, the portico of judgment, and covered it with fir wood from floor to floor.
His house, where he would live, had a vaulted courtyard made in the same manner. The house for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom Solomon had married, was also vaulted according to the same design.
Everything was made of costly stones, hewn to size and fitted together with [?], inside and outside, from the foundation to the ceiling, and outside as far as the great courtyard.
The foundation was laid with very large stones, stones ten cubits long and stones eight cubits long.
Above them were costly dressed stones of the same dimensions, and fir wood.

The great courtyard had three courses of dressed stone all around and one course joined together with fir wood. He also built the inner courtyard of the house of the Lord, by the porticoes of the house of the Lord, opposite the temple.
King Solomon sent for Hiram and brought him from Tyre.

He was the son of a widow and belonged to the tribe of Naphtali. His father was a Tyrian, a craftsman in bronze. He was full of skill, wisdom, and knowledge for doing every kind of bronze work. He came to King Solomon and did all the work.

He cast the two pillars for the portico of the house. One pillar was eighteen cubits high and measured fourteen cubits in circumference. The pillar was four fingerbreadths thick, with [?]. The second pillar was the same.
He made two capitals of cast bronze to place on top of the pillars. One capital was five cubits high, and the second capital was five cubits high.
He made two lattices to cover the first capital, and he made two more lattices to cover the second capital, with hanging ornamentation.
For both pillars he made bronze pomegranates on the latticework, with hanging ornamentation, row upon row. He did the same for the second capital.
On top of the pillars in the portico was lily-shaped work, four cubits high.
And there was a molding above both pillars, at the top; along the sides of the capital was a molding, and two hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments in rows around the second capital.
And he erected the pillars at the archway of the temple. He erected the first pillar and named it Jachin, and he erected the second pillar and named it Boaz.
And on top of the pillars was lily-shaped work, and the work on the pillars was completed.
And he made the cast-metal sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, uniformly round in shape. Its height was five cubits, and its circumference measured thirty-three cubits all around.
And supports beneath it encircled it for ten cubits all around. Two rows of posts were cast as part of its casting and fixed in place.
And twelve oxen were beneath the sea: three faced north, three faced the sea, three faced south, and three faced east. The sea rested above them, and all their hindquarters faced inward.
And its thickness was a handbreadth, and its brim was worked like the brim of a cup, with a lily blossom upon it. It held about two thousand measures.
And he made ten bronze stands. Each stand was five cubits long, four cubits wide, and six cubits high.
And this was the construction of the stands: panels above, and panels between the axles.
On their panels, between the supports, were lions, bulls, and cherubim, and likewise on the supports above. Below the lions and bulls were spaces with [?] work.
And each stand had four bronze wheels and bronze axles. At their four corners were supports beneath the basins, and the cast supports resembled human attendants standing alongside.

And its opening was inside the capital and extended one cubit upward. Its opening was likewise round in construction, and its thickness was a cubit and a half. At its opening was firmly fixed, lathe-turned work, square and not round.
And the four wheels were beneath the fixed supports, and the wheel axles were attached to the stands. The height of each wheel was a cubit and a half.
And the construction of the wheels was like the construction of chariot wheels. Their axles, their hubs, their rims, and all their parts were cast.
There were four supports at the four corners of each stand; its supports were part of the stand itself.
And at the top of the stand was a large circular rim, half a cubit high, surrounding it. The tops of its arms and its panels were made as part of the stand itself.
And on the tops of its arms and on its panels they carved cherubim, lions, and palm trees standing alongside it, each on its corresponding face, on the inside and all around.
According to this same pattern he made all ten stands, all with one form, one size, and one design.
And he made ten bronze washing basins. Each basin held forty jarfuls, and each basin measured four cubits. There was one basin on each of the ten stands.
And he placed five stands on the right side of the house and five on the left side of the house. He placed the sea on the right side of the house, toward the east, on the southern side.
And Hiram made the pots, the firepans, and the bowls. Hiram finished making all the work that he made for King Solomon in the house of the Lord:
the two pillars, the two rounded capitals of the carved pillars on top of the pillars, and the two latticeworks to cover the two rounded carved capitals that were on top of the pillars;

the four hundred pomegranate-shaped ornaments for the two latticeworks, two rows of pomegranate-shaped ornaments for each latticework, to cover the two rounded moldings of the stands above the two pillars;
and the stands, and the ten washing basins upon the stands;
and the one sea, and the twelve oxen beneath the sea.

And the cauldrons, the heating vessels, [?], the basins, and all the furnishings that Hiram made for King Solomon in the house of the Lord, and forty-eight pillars for the king’s house and the house of the Lord—Hiram completed all the king’s work entirely in bronze. The bronze from which he made all these objects could not be weighed because of its immense quantity; there was no measure of the weight of the gleaming bronze.
On the bank of the Jordan, in the thick soil between Succoth and Zarethan, he cast these things for the king.
And King Solomon gave [?] for all the furnishings, for they were exceedingly numerous, and there was no count of the bronze.
And Solomon made all the furnishings for the house of the Lord: the golden altar and the golden table on which the bread of offering lay,
and the lampstands, five on the right and five on the left, facing the inner sanctuary, of pure gold, and the holders, the lamps, and the trimmers of gold,
and the doorframes, the nails, the basins, the bowls, and the boxes of pure gold, and the golden doors of the inner house, the Holy of Holies, and the doors of the temple building.

And all the work that King Solomon did for the house of the Lord was completed. King Solomon brought in the things dedicated by David his father and all the things dedicated by Solomon, and he placed the silver, the gold, and the furnishings in the treasuries of the house of the Lord.

Then King Solomon assembled all the elders of Israel, together with all the heads of the tribes, the leaders of the ancestral families of the Israelites, before King Solomon in Zion, to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord from the city of David, which is Zion.
And all the men of Israel assembled before King Solomon in the month of Ethanim, at the festival, which is in the seventh month.
And all the elders of Israel went up, and the priests took up the ark.
And they brought up the ark of the Lord, the tent of testimony, and all the sacred utensils that were in the tent of testimony. The priests and the Levites brought them up.
And King Solomon and all the congregation of Israel gathered before him were with him before the ark, sacrificing cattle and sheep too numerous to count or number.
And the priests brought the ark of the covenant of the Lord inside to its place, into the inner sanctuary of the house, the Holy of Holies, beneath the wings of the cherubim.
For the cherubim had their wings spread over the place of the ark, and the cherubim covered the ark and its sacred objects from above.

And they rested upon the consecrated objects, and the ends of the consecrated objects could be seen from the sanctuary in front of the inner sanctuary, but they were not visible outside. And they remained there to this day.

And there was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant, which Moses placed there at Horeb, when the Lord made a covenant with the Israelites as they came out of the land of the Egyptians.
And when the priests came out of the sanctuary, the cloud filled the house of the Lord.
The priests could not stand to minister because of the cloud, for the glory of the Lord filled the house.
Then Solomon said, “The Lord said that he would dwell under the cover of a dark cloud.
I have indeed built you a house to dwell in, an established place for your throne forever.”
And the king turned his face and blessed all Israel, while the whole assembly of Israel stood.
And he said, “Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, today, who spoke with his mouth concerning David my father and fulfilled it with his hands, saying,

‘From the day when I brought my people Israel out of Egypt, I did not choose any city among the tribes of Israel in which to build a house for my name to be there, but I chose David to be over my people Israel.’
And it was in the heart of David my father to build a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
And the Lord said to David my father, ‘Because it came into your heart to build a house for my name, you did well to have this in your heart.
But you shall not build the house. Rather, your son, who will come from your loins, will build the house for my name.’

And the Lord fulfilled the word he had spoken. I have succeeded David my father and sat on the throne of Israel, just as the Lord said, and I have built a house for the name of the Lord, the God of Israel.
And I provided a place there for the ark, which is the covenant of the Lord that the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of the Egyptians.
And Solomon stood before the altar of the Lord, in front of the whole assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven.
And he said, “Lord, God of Israel, there is no God like you in heaven above or on earth below. You have kept your covenant and shown mercy to your servant who walked before you with all his heart.
You have kept what you promised to your servant David my father. You spoke with your mouth and fulfilled it with your hands, as it is this day.

And now, Lord, God of Israel, keep for your servant David my father what you told him when you said, ‘You will never lack a man before me to sit on the throne of Israel, provided that your sons take care how they walk, walking before me as you walked before me.’
And now, Lord, God of Israel, let the word you spoke to your servant David my father prove true.
Will God dwell with human beings on earth? If heaven and the heaven of heavens cannot contain you, how can this house that I have built?
And now, attend to your servant’s prayer and my petitions, Lord, God of Israel. Hear the pleas and prayers of your servant, who stands before you and addresses you.
Let your eyes be open night and day toward this place, of which you said, ‘My name will be there,’ to hear the prayers that your servant offers in this place by day and by night.
And hear the voice of your servant and of your people Israel when they stand in prayer in this place. Hear them in your dwelling place in heaven,
and act and forgive. Whenever anyone sins against his neighbor, and a curse is laid upon him to curse him, and he makes a confession before your altar in this house,

hear from heaven, act, and judge your people Israel, condemning the wicked by bringing his conduct down upon his own head, and vindicating the righteous by rewarding him according to his righteousness.

And when your people Israel are defeated before their enemies because they have sinned against you, and they turn back to you, acknowledge your name, stand in prayer, and plead with you in this house,
hear from heaven, forgive the sins of your people Israel, and bring them back to the land you gave their fathers.
And when heaven is shut and there is no rain because they have sinned against you, and they stand in prayer in this place, acknowledge your name, and turn from their sins when you humble them,

hear from heaven and forgive the sins of your servants and your people Israel, so that you may show them the good way to walk in. Give rain upon your land, which you gave your people as an inheritance.
And if there is famine in the land, or pestilence, or scorching blight, or mildew, or locusts, or rust, or if their enemy besieges them in one of their cities—whatever the calamity or disease—
whatever prayer or petition is offered by anyone among all your people Israel, as each one recognizes the affliction of his own heart and spreads out his hands toward this house,

And may you hear from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and forgive and act, and give to each man according to all his ways, as you know his heart, for you alone know the heart of all human beings.
So that they may fear you all their days, as long as they live on the face of the earth that you gave to our fathers.
And also the foreigner who is not of your people Israel and comes from a distant land,
where he hears of your great name and your mighty hand and your outstretched arm, and comes and stands in prayer in this place—

may you hear from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and do everything for which the foreigner calls upon you, so that all the nations of the earth may know your name and fear you, as your people Israel do, and know that your name is invoked over this house that I have built.

And if your people go out to war against their enemies along the route by which you direct them, and stand in prayer in the name of the Lord, facing this city that you have chosen and this house that I have built for your name,
may you hear their prayers and their pleas from heaven and uphold their cause.

For they will sin against you, since there is no one who does not sin; and if you turn against them and hand them over to their enemies, and their captors carry them away to an enemy’s land, far away or nearby,
And if they turn their hearts in the land where they were taken captive, and turn back and plead with you in the land of their captivity, saying, ‘We have sinned, acted lawlessly, and done wrong,’

and return to you with all their heart and all their soul in the land of their enemies, where you have sent them, and stand in prayer to you facing their land, which you gave to their fathers, and this city that you have chosen and the house that I have built for your name,
may you hear their prayers and their pleas from heaven, from your established dwelling place, and uphold their cause.

And may you forgive their wrongdoing by which they sinned against you, and all the acts of contempt by which they treated you with contempt, and grant them compassion in the sight of their captors, and have compassion on them.
For they are your people and your inheritance, whom you brought out of the land of the Egyptians, from the midst of the iron-smelting furnace.
And may your eyes and your ears be open to the pleas of your servant and the pleas of your people Israel, to hear them whenever they call upon you.

For you set them apart for yourself as an inheritance from all the peoples of the earth, as you spoke through Moses your servant when you brought our fathers out of Egypt, O Lord, Lord. Then Solomon spoke about the house when he had finished building it: ‘He made the sun known in heaven. The Lord said he would dwell in darkness. Build my house, a splendid house to dwell in anew.’ Is this not written there in the Book of Songs?

And when Solomon had finished offering all this prayer and these pleas to the Lord, he rose from before the altar of the Lord, where he had been kneeling on his knees with his hands spread out toward heaven.
He stood and blessed the whole assembly of Israel in a loud voice, saying:
‘Blessed is the Lord today, who has given rest to his people Israel according to everything he said. Not one word has failed of all his good words that he spoke through Moses his servant.
May the Lord our God be with us as he was with our fathers, and may he not abandon us,
but turn us so that our hearts do not turn away from him, to walk in all his ways and keep all his commandments, his decrees, and his judgments, which he commanded our fathers.

May these words of mine, with which I pleaded before the Lord our God, be near the Lord our God day and night, to uphold the cause of your servant and the cause of your people Israel, as each day requires.’
So that all the peoples of the earth may know that the Lord is God and there is no other.
And may our hearts be wholly devoted to the Lord our God, walking blamelessly according to his decrees and keeping his commandments, as on this day.
And the king and all the Israelites with him offered sacrifices before the Lord.
And King Solomon offered peace offerings to the Lord: twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. Thus the king and all the Israelites dedicated the house of the Lord.

On that day the king consecrated the middle of the courtyard in front of the house of the Lord, for there he offered the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, the sacrifices, and the fat of the peace offerings. For the bronze altar that stood before the Lord was small and could not hold the burnt offerings, the grain offerings, and the peace offerings.

And on that day Solomon held a feast, and all Israel with him, a great assembly from the entrance of Hamath to the river of Egypt, before the Lord our God, in the house he had built. They ate and drank and rejoiced before the Lord our God for seven days and another seven days—fourteen days.

And on the eighth day he dismissed the people. They blessed the king and went, each to their own dwelling, joyful and glad at heart because of all the good that the Lord had done for his servant David and for his people Israel.
And when Solomon had finished building the house of the Lord and the king’s house, and all the works that Solomon wished to carry out,
the Lord appeared to Solomon a second time, as he had appeared to him at Gibeon.

And the Lord said to him, “I have heard your prayer and the pleas you made before me. I have done for you according to all your prayers. I have consecrated the house you built, to put my name there forever, and my eyes and my heart will be there always.
And if you walk before me as your father David walked, with a pure heart and uprightness, doing everything I commanded him, and keeping my decrees and my commandments,
I will establish the throne of your kingdom over Israel forever, as I spoke to your father David, saying, ‘You shall never lack a man to rule over Israel.’
But if you and your children turn away from me and do not keep my commandments and my decrees, which Moses set before you, and go and serve foreign gods and worship them,
I will remove Israel from the land I gave them, and this house, which I consecrated for my name, I will cast out of my sight. Israel will become a ruin and a subject of talk among all peoples.
And this house will be held up as a byword. Everyone who passes by it will be astonished and hiss and say, ‘Why has the Lord done this to this land and this house?’

And they will say, ‘Because they abandoned the Lord their God, who brought their fathers out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery, and embraced foreign gods and worshiped them and served them. That is why the Lord brought all these calamities upon them.’” Then Solomon brought Pharaoh’s daughter up from the city of David to his own house, which he had built for himself.
And in those days, during the twenty years in which Solomon built the two houses—the house of the Lord and the king’s house—
Hiram king of Tyre supplied Solomon with fir wood, cedar wood, gold, and everything he wanted. Then King Solomon gave Hiram twenty towns in Galilee.
Hiram left Tyre and went to Galilee to see the cities Solomon had given him, and they did not please him.
And he said, “What are these cities you have given me, my brother?” And he called them “the Districts,” as they are called to this day.
And Hiram brought Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold.

These are the details of the levy that King Solomon raised to build the house of the Lord, the king’s house, Millo, and the raised terraces, to fill in the trenches of the City of David, and to build Asshur, Maidan, the wall of Jerusalem, Ezer, Megiddo, and Gezer,
of Pharaoh, king of Egypt. For he went up and captured Gezer, burned it with fire, killed the Canaanites who lived in the city, and gave it as a dowry to his daughter, Solomon’s wife.
And Solomon rebuilt Gezer and Lower Beth-horon,
And Baalath and Thermoth in the wilderness, in that land.
and all the towns for settlement that belonged to Solomon, the towns for chariots, all the towns for horses, and whatever Solomon planned to build in Jerusalem, in Lebanon, and throughout the land,
because he did not have authority over all the people who remained from the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, Canaanites, Jebusites, and Girgashites, who were not Israelites.
Their descendants remained after them in the land, and the Israelites had been unable to destroy them. Solomon subjected them to compulsory labor, as they remain to this day.
But Solomon did not assign any of the Israelites to forced labor, because they were his warriors, his servants, his commanders, his armed troops, and his horsemen.
These were the officials in charge of Solomon’s work: five hundred and fifty, who supervised the people doing the work.
But Pharaoh’s daughter went up from the City of David to her own house, which he had built for her. Then he built the Millo.
Three times a year Solomon offered burnt offerings and peace offerings on the altar he had built for the Lord, and he burned incense before the Lord.
And he completed the house. King Solomon built a ship at Ezion-geber, which is near Elath, on the shore of the farthest sea, in the land of Edom.
Hiram sent some of his servants with the ships—sailors experienced in navigating the sea—along with Solomon’s servants.
They went to Ophir, obtained four hundred and twenty talents of gold there, and brought it to King Solomon.
And the queen of Sheba heard of Solomon’s fame, the name of the Lord, and Solomon’s wisdom, and she came to test him with riddles.

She came to Jerusalem with a very large retinue and camels carrying spices, a very great quantity of gold, and precious stones. She came to Solomon and spoke with him about everything that was in her heart.
Solomon explained all her questions to her. Nothing escaped the king that he could not explain to her.
The queen saw all Solomon’s wisdom and the houses he had built,
Solomon’s food, the seating of his servants, the arrangement of his attendants, his clothing, his cupbearers, and the burnt offerings he offered to the Lord, and she was bewildered.
She said to King Solomon, “The report I heard in my land about your words and your wisdom was true.
I did not believe those who spoke to me until I came myself and my own eyes saw it. Look, they did not tell me even half of it: your wisdom and prosperity surpass all the reports I heard in my land.
Happy are your wives, and happy are your servants who stand before you and continually hear your wisdom!

Blessed be the Lord your God, who delighted in you and placed you on the throne of Israel! Because the Lord loved Israel and wished to establish it forever, he made you king over them to administer justice and righteousness in their courts.”

She gave Solomon one hundred and twenty talents of gold, a very great quantity of spices, and precious stones. No spices had ever arrived in such abundance and with such fragrance as those the queen of Sheba gave King Solomon.
Hiram’s ship, which brought gold from Ophir, also brought a very great quantity of unhewn timber and precious stones from Ophir.

The king made the unhewn timber into supports for the house of the Lord and the king’s house, and into lyres and harps for the singers. Such unhewn timber had never come into the land or been seen anywhere to this day.
King Solomon gave the queen of Sheba everything she desired and requested, besides what had been given to her through King Solomon. Then she returned to her own land, together with all her servants.
The weight of the gold that came to Solomon in one year was six hundred and sixty-six talents of gold,
apart from the appointed taxes, the merchants’ trade, and what came from all the kings of that region and the governors of the land.
King Solomon made three hundred spears of beaten gold, with three hundred darics used for each spear,
and three hundred shields of beaten gold, with three minas of gold used for each shield. The king placed them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.
The king made a great ivory throne and covered it with refined gold.
The throne had six steps, with the faces of oxen at the back of the throne, and armrests on either side of the seat. Two lions stood beside the armrests.
Twelve lions stood on the six steps, on either side. Nothing like it had been made in any kingdom.

All King Solomon’s serving vessels were made of gold, and the basins were gold. All the furnishings of the House of the Forest of Lebanon were covered with gold. There was no silver, because silver was considered of no value in Solomon’s days.
For King Solomon had a ship of Tarshish at sea with Hiram’s ships, and every three years a ship came to the king from Tarshish, bringing gold, silver, elephants’ tusks, apes, and peacocks.
Solomon surpassed all the kings of the earth in greatness and wisdom.
All the kings of the earth sought to see Solomon’s face and hear the wisdom that the Lord had put in his heart.
Each of them brought his gifts: silver vessels, gold vessels, garments, stacte, incense, horses, and mules, year after year.

Solomon gathered chariots and horsemen. Solomon had forty thousand mares for chariots and twelve thousand steeds. He stationed them in the chariot cities and with the king in Jerusalem. He ruled over all the kings from the River to the Philistines and to the borders of Egypt.
The king made silver and gold as plentiful as stones in Jerusalem, and fir timber as plentiful as the sycamore trees in the plains.
Solomon’s horses came from Egypt and Tekoa, and the king’s merchants bought them in Tekoa for a price.

Chariots were brought out of Egypt in exchange for silver, and a horse for one hundred and fifty pieces of silver. In the same way they were exported along the coast for all the kings of the Hittites and the kings of the Syrians.
King Solomon loved women and took many foreign wives, including Pharaoh’s daughter, Moabite women, Ammonite women, Edomite women, Syrian women, Hittite women, and Amorite women.

They were from the nations concerning which the Lord had instructed the Israelites, “You must not join with them, nor may they join with you, lest they turn your hearts aside to follow their idols.” Solomon clung to these women in love.
He had seven hundred wives of royal rank and three hundred concubines, and his wives turned his heart aside.
When Solomon was old, his wives turned his heart aside to follow foreign gods, and his heart was not fully devoted to the Lord his God, as the heart of his father David had been.
And Solomon followed Ashtoreth, the abomination of the Sidonians, and Milcom, the abomination of the Ammonites.
And Solomon did evil before the Lord and did not follow the Lord as his father David had.
Then Solomon built the high place for Chemosh, the idol of Moab, on the mountain opposite Jerusalem, and for Molech, the idol of the Ammonites, and for Ashtoreth, the abomination of the Sidonians.
And he did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and sacrificed to their idols.
And the Lord became angry with Solomon because he had turned his heart away from the Lord, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
and had commanded him concerning this matter not to follow foreign gods at all, and to keep and carry out what the Lord God had commanded him.

And the Lord said to Solomon, “Because this has happened with you, and you have not kept my ordinances and the commandments that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from your hand and give it to your servant.
But I will not do this in your lifetime, for the sake of David your father; instead, I will take it from the hand of your son.
Yet I will not take away the whole kingdom. I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I chose.”
And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Hadad the Edomite, from the royal family of the Edomites.
And it happened when David was destroying Edom, when Joab, the commander of the army, went to bury the wounded, for they had killed every male in Edom.
For Joab and all Israel stayed there in Edom for six months, until he had destroyed every male among the Edomites.
And Hadad himself and all the Edomite men who were servants of his father fled and went into Egypt. Hadad was a small child.

And the men set out from the city of Midian and came to Paran. They took men from Paran with them and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. Hadad went in to Pharaoh, who gave him a house, provided him with food, and gave him land.
And Hadad found great favor with Pharaoh, who gave him as his wife the sister of his own wife, the elder sister of Tahpenes.
And the sister of Tahpenes bore Hadad his son Genubath. Tahpenes raised him among Pharaoh’s sons, and Genubath was in Pharaoh’s house among Pharaoh’s sons.
And Hadad heard in Egypt that David had fallen asleep with his fathers and that Joab, the commander of the army, had died. Hadad said to Pharaoh, “Let me go, so that I may return to my own land.”
And Pharaoh said to Hadad, “What do you lack here with me, that you seek to go to your own land?” Hadad said to him, “Just be sure to let me go.” And Hadad returned to his own land.
And the Lord raised up an adversary against Solomon: Rezon son of Eliada, who had fled from his master, Hadadezer king of Zobah.
And men gathered around him, and he was the leader of the band when David was killing them. They went to Damascus and settled there, and he reigned in Damascus.
And he was an adversary of Israel throughout all the days of Solomon. This was the evil done by Hadad, and there was fierce anger against Israel, and he reigned in the land of Edom.
And Jeroboam son of Nebat, an Ephrathite from Zeredah—his mother’s name was Zeruah, a widow, and he was the son of a widowed woman—was Solomon’s servant, and he raised his hand against the king.
And these were the circumstances in which he raised his hand against King Solomon: Solomon built the terrace and filled in the breach in the city of David his father.
And the man Jeroboam was mighty in strength. When Solomon saw that the young man was capable in his work, he put him in charge of the forced labor of the burden-bearers of the house of Joseph.

And it happened at that time that Jeroboam went out from Jerusalem, and the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite met him on the road and took him aside from the road. Ahijah was wearing a new garment, and the two of them were in the field.
And Ahijah took hold of his new garment that he was wearing and tore it into twelve pieces.
And he said to Jeroboam, “Take ten of these pieces for yourself, for thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: ‘Look, I will tear the kingdom from Solomon’s hands and give you the ten tribes.’”
And he shall have two tribes, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city I chose from among all the tribes of Israel.

Because he abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth, the abomination of the Sidonians, Chemosh, the idol of Moab, and Milcom, the detestable god of the Ammonites, and did not walk in my ways, doing what is right before me and keeping my statutes and my judgments, as David his father did.

And I will not take the whole kingdom from his hand, for I will stand in opposition against him all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant, whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.
And I will take the kingdom from his hand and give you the ten tribes.
And I will give his son the two tribes, so that my servant David may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city I chose to put my name there.
And I will take you, and you shall reign over whatever your heart desires, and you shall be king over Israel.

And if you keep everything I command you, walk in my ways, and do what is right before me, carefully observing my commandments and my decrees, as David my servant did, I will be with you and build you an enduring house, as I built for David, and I will give you Israel.
And I will afflict David’s descendants because of this, but not forever.
And Solomon sought to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam arose and fled to Egypt, to Shishak king of the Egyptians, and remained in Egypt until Solomon died.
Now the rest of Solomon’s deeds, everything he did, and all his wisdom—are they not written in the book of the deeds of Solomon?
And the time Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
And Solomon slept with his ancestors, and they buried him in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
And King Rehoboam went to Shechem, because all Israel was coming to Shechem to make him king.
And when Jeroboam son of Nebat heard of it—he was still in Egypt, where he had fled from King Solomon—Jeroboam returned from Egypt.
And they sent for him and called him, and Jeroboam and the whole assembly of Israel came. And all the people spoke to King Rehoboam, saying:
“Your father made our yoke heavy. Now lighten your father’s harsh burden and the heavy yoke he placed upon us, and we will serve you.”
And he said to them, “Go away for three days, and return to me.” And they went away.
And King Rehoboam consulted the elders who had served before Solomon his father while he was alive, and said, “What do you advise? What answer should we give these people?”
And they spoke to him, saying, “If today you become a servant to these people and serve them, listen to them, and speak good words to them, they will be your servants forever.”
But he abandoned the advice of the elders whom he had consulted, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him and served before him.
And he said to them, “What advice do you give? What answer should I give these people who spoke to me, saying, ‘Lighten the yoke your father placed upon us’?”

And the young men who had grown up with him and served before him spoke to him, saying, “This is what you should say in the hearing of these people who spoke to you, saying, ‘Your father made our yoke heavy, but you must lighten it for us.’ Say this to them: ‘My little finger is thicker than my father’s waist.’”
And now, my father placed a heavy yoke on you, and I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.
And all Israel came to King Rehoboam on the third day, as the king had told them, saying, “Return to me on the third day.”
The king answered the people harshly, and Rehoboam rejected the advice that the elders had given him.

He spoke to them according to the advice of the young men and said, “My father made your yoke heavy, and I will add to your yoke. My father disciplined you with whips, but I will discipline you with scorpions.”

And the king did not listen to the people, for this turn of events was from the Lord, so that the Lord might establish his word, which he had spoken through Ahijah the Shilonite concerning Jeroboam son of Nebat.

When all Israel saw that the king had not listened to them, the people answered the king, saying, “What share do we have in David? We have no inheritance in the son of Jesse. Back to your homes, Israel! Now look after the house of David yourself.” And Israel went to their homes.
But Rehoboam reigned over the Israelites who lived in the cities of Judah.
King Rehoboam sent Adoniram, the overseer of forced labor, and all Israel stoned him to death. King Rehoboam hurried to climb into his chariot and flee to Jerusalem.
And Israel rejected the house of David, as it does to this day.

When all Israel heard that Jeroboam had returned, they sent for him, called him to the assembly, and made him king over Israel. No one followed the house of David except the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.

Rehoboam came to Jerusalem and assembled the people of Judah and the tribe of Benjamin, one hundred and eighty thousand young fighting men, to fight against the house of Israel and restore the kingdom to Rehoboam son of Solomon.
The word of the Lord came to Shemaiah, the man of God, saying:
“Speak to Rehoboam son of Solomon, king of Judah, to all the house of Judah and Benjamin, and to the rest of the people, and say:

‘This is what the Lord says: Do not go up or fight against your brothers, the Israelites. Let everyone return to his own home, for this has come about through me.’” They listened to the word of the Lord and stopped their advance, according to the word of the Lord.
Jeroboam built Shechem in the hill country of Ephraim and lived there. He went out from there and built Penuel.
Jeroboam said in his heart, “Now my kingdom will return to the house of David.

If these people go up to offer sacrifices in the house of the Lord in Jerusalem, the hearts of these people will turn to the Lord and to their master, Rehoboam king of Judah. They will kill me and return to Rehoboam king of Judah.”

The king took counsel, went and made two golden heifers, and said to the people, “You have gone up to Jerusalem long enough. Here are your gods, Israel, who brought you up from the land of the Egyptians.”
He placed one in Bethel and the other in Dan.
This became a sin, and the people went before one of them as far as Dan.
He built shrines on the high places and appointed priests from among the people who were not of the house of Levi.

Jeroboam established a festival in the eighth month, on the fifteenth day of that month, like the festival in the land of Judah. He went up to the altar he had made in Bethel to sacrifice to the heifers he had made, and he stationed in Bethel priests for the high places he had made.

He went up to the altar he had made in Bethel on the fifteenth day of the eighth month, during the festival he had devised in his own heart. He established a festival for the Israelites and went up to the altar to offer sacrifice.
And behold, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel by the word of the Lord, while Jeroboam was standing at his altar to offer sacrifice on it.

And he cried out to the altar by the word of the Lord and said, “Altar, altar, this is what the Lord says: Look, a son will be born to the house of David, Josiah by name, and he will sacrifice on you the priests of the high places who offer sacrifices on you, and human bones will be burned on you.”
And that day he gave a sign and said, “This is the sign that the Lord has spoken of: Look, the altar will split apart, and the fat on it will be poured out.”

When King Jeroboam heard the words of the man of God crying out against the altar in Bethel, the king stretched out his hand from the altar and said, “Seize him!” And the hand he stretched out toward him withered, and he could not draw it back to himself.
And the altar split apart, and the fat was poured out from the altar, according to the sign that the man of God had given by the word of the Lord.

And King Jeroboam said to the man of God, “Please seek the favor of the Lord your God and pray for me, so that my hand may be restored to me.” And the man of God pleaded before the Lord, and the king’s hand was restored to him and became as it had been before.
And the king spoke to the man of God and said, “Come home with me and eat, and I will give you a gift.”
And the man of God said to the king, “Even if you give me half your house, I will not come in with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place,
for this is what the Lord commanded me by his word: ‘Do not eat bread or drink water, and do not go back by the same road you take.’”
And he went on his way, but he did not leave Bethel by the same road by which he had come.
Now an old prophet lived in Bethel, and his sons came and told him everything the man of God had done that day in Bethel, and the words he had spoken to the king; and they turned their father’s face.
And their father spoke to them and said, “Which road did he take?” And his sons showed him the road taken by the man of God who had come from Judah.
And he said to his sons, “Saddle the donkey.” And they saddled a donkey for him, and he mounted it.
And he went after the man of God and found him sitting under the oak. He said to him, “Are you the man of God who came from Judah?” And he said, “I am.”
And he said to him, “Come home with me and eat bread.”
And he said, “I cannot return with you or come with you, nor will I eat bread or drink water in this place,
for this is the command given to me by the word of the Lord: ‘Do not eat bread or drink water there, and do not return by the same road you take.’”

And he said to him, “I too am a prophet like you, and an angel of the Lord spoke to me and said, ‘Bring him back with you to your house, so that he may eat bread and drink water.’” But he lied to him.
And he brought him back with him, and he ate bread in his house and drank water.
And while they were sitting at the table, the word of the Lord came to the prophet who had brought him back,

and he spoke to the man of God who had come from Judah and said, “This is what the Lord says: Because you rebelled against the word of the Lord and did not keep the command that the Lord your God gave you,
but returned and ate bread and drank water in this place, about which he told you, ‘Do not eat bread or drink water,’ your body shall not enter the tomb of your fathers.”
And after he had eaten bread and drunk water, he saddled the donkey for the prophet.
And he turned and went away, and a lion found him on the road and killed him. His body lay on the road, and the donkey stood beside it, and the lion stood beside the body.
And some men passing by saw the dead man lying on the road, with the lion standing beside him, and they went into the city where the old prophet lived and told what they had seen.

When the one who had brought him back from the road heard this, he said, “That is the man of God who rebelled against the word of the Lord. The Lord gave him over to the lion, which tore him apart and killed him, according to the word the Lord had spoken to him.”
And he spoke to his sons and said, “Saddle the donkey.” And they saddled it.
He went and found his body lying on the road, with the donkey and the lion standing beside the body. The lion had neither eaten the body of the man of God nor mauled the donkey.
The prophet took the body of the man of God, put it on the donkey, and brought it back. He came to the old prophet’s city to mourn for him and bury him.
The prophet laid his body in his own tomb to bury him. They mourned for him and said, “Alas, my brother!”

After mourning for him, he spoke to his sons and said, “When I die, bury me in this tomb where the man of God was buried. Lay me beside his bones, so that my bones may be preserved along with his bones.
For the message he spoke by the word of the Lord against the altar in Bethel and against the shrines on the high places in Samaria will certainly come true.”

Even after these things, Jeroboam did not turn away from his evil ways. He again made priests for the high places from among the people. Whoever wished could be ordained and become a priest of the high places.
This became a sin for the house of Jeroboam, leading to its destruction and removal from the face of the earth.
At that time Abijah, the son of Jeroboam, became ill.

Jeroboam said to his wife, “Get up and disguise yourself, so that no one will know you are Jeroboam’s wife, and go to Shiloh. Ahijah the prophet is there. He said that I would reign over this people.”
And take in your hand bread for the man of God, cakes for his sons, raisins, and a jar of honey, and go to him. He will tell you what will happen to the child.
Jeroboam’s wife did so. She got up, went to Shiloh, and entered Ahijah’s house. The man could no longer see, for his eyes had grown weak with age.
The Lord said to Ahijah, “Jeroboam’s wife is coming to ask you about her son, for he is ill. You shall say such and such to her.” When she came in, she was pretending to be someone else.

When Ahijah heard the sound of her footsteps as she came in and opened the door, he said, “Come in, Jeroboam’s wife. Why are you pretending to be someone else? I have been sent to you with a harsh message.
Go and say to Jeroboam, “Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: Because I raised you up from among the people and made you ruler over my people Israel,

I tore the kingdom away from the house of David and gave it to you. Yet you have not been like my servant David, who kept my commandments and followed me with all his heart, doing what was right before me.
You have done more evil than all who were before you. You went and made yourself foreign gods and cast idols to provoke me to anger, and you cast me behind your back.

Therefore I will bring disaster upon the house of Jeroboam. I will destroy every male belonging to Jeroboam, whether confined or free in Israel. I will sweep away the remnants of the house of Jeroboam as dung is swept away, until it is all gone.
The dogs will eat those belonging to Jeroboam who die in the city, and the birds of the sky will eat those who die in the open country, for the Lord has spoken.
Now get up and go to your house. When your feet enter the city, the child will die.

All Israel will mourn for him and bury him. He alone of Jeroboam’s family will be laid in a tomb, because in the house of Jeroboam he alone was found to have something good toward the Lord, the God of Israel.
The Lord will raise up for himself a king over Israel who will strike down the house of Jeroboam this very day. And now, what more?

The Lord will strike Israel, so that it shakes like a reed in the water. The Lord will uproot Israel from this good land that he gave to their fathers and scatter them beyond the River, because they made themselves sacred groves, provoking the Lord to anger.
The Lord will give Israel over because of the sins of Jeroboam, who sinned and caused Israel to sin.”
